title: Distribution live read loop allocates a peer-sized frame with an infallible allocator — a max-frame cap at both framing sites
purpose:
Ground: finding H6 of the 2026-07-23 whole-repository review (`docs/REVIEW-23-07.md:71-73`, reviewed at beamr `fd71c5e`). Queue position: RF-003 follows RF-001 (top of the dispatch queue) and sits with RF-002 in the untrusted-input DoS band the review groups as priority 4. The defect: the live distribution read loop takes two full `u32` lengths straight off the wire, guards only the `checked_add` overflow, and then allocates `vec![0_u8; total_len]` with the INFALLIBLE allocator. Eight bytes of peer input become a multi-gigabyte zeroed commit, or `handle_alloc_error` aborts the entire host process — taking down every other connection, every scheduler and every process in the node, not just the offending link.

HOSTILE-PEER FRAMING — BOUNDS BUT DOES NOT EXCUSE: this code path runs only AFTER the handshake. `spawn_read_lifecycle` (`crates/beamr/src/distribution/connection.rs:1432`) is reached exactly once, from `register_connection` at `:1367`, which runs after `initiate_handshake_async` / `respond_handshake_async_with` have authenticated the peer against the shared cookie. So the attacker must be a cookie-holding node, not an arbitrary internet host. That narrows the population; it does not narrow the blast radius. In a mesh, ONE compromised or buggy peer aborts every node it can dial, and a distribution cookie is a shared secret across a cluster, not a per-peer credential. "Authenticated" is not "trusted" — this is the same threat model under which the loader is already systematically hardened (`loader/decode/budget.rs`).

RE-PIN AT a0359a2 (review line numbers checked against current main; NO DRIFT on either cited site):
- CITED SITE `distribution/connection.rs:1477` → EXACT, `let mut frame = vec![0_u8; total_len];`. Surrounding, all re-read: `spawn_read_lifecycle` fn `:1432`; the 8-byte header read `:1451-1461` (raced against shutdown via `tokio::select!`); `control_len` from `header[0..4]` `:1467-1469`; `payload_len` from `header[4..8]` `:1470-1472`; the `checked_add` overflow guard `:1473-1476` (marks down `ReadError` and breaks); `read_half.read_exact(&mut frame)` `:1478`; the control-frame handler dispatch `:1483-1490` splitting `frame.split_at(control_len)`.
- CITED SAFE PATTERN `distribution/etf.rs:151` → EXACT. `read_dist_message` fn `:146`; `let length = usize::try_from(u32::from_be_bytes(header)).map_err(|_| Error::LengthTooLarge)?` `:148`; `let mut body = Vec::new();` `:149`; `body.try_reserve_exact(length)` `:150`; `.map_err(|_| Error::LengthTooLarge)?` `:151`; `body.resize(length, 0)` `:152`.
- MATERIAL FINDING 1 — THE CITED SAFE PATTERN IS DEAD CODE ON THE LIVE PATH. `read_dist_message` has ZERO non-test callers in the workspace (its only callers are the tests in `distribution/etf.rs` itself, `:1300-1339`). The live loop is `connection.rs`. So this is not "copy the neighbour": the neighbour is unexercised in production and is itself defective (below).
- MATERIAL FINDING 2 — `try_reserve_exact` IS NOT A CAP. It converts an allocator ABORT into a graceful `Err`, but a 4 GiB reservation the allocator CAN satisfy still succeeds. `read_dist_message` reads the same peer-controlled `u32` with no ceiling, so `etf.rs:148-152` is the SAME defect with a milder failure mode. The cap must land at BOTH sites; treating `etf.rs` as already-correct would leave the framing helper unbounded the moment anything starts calling it.
- MATERIAL FINDING 3 — ZERO-LENGTH FRAMES ARE THE KEEPALIVE. `KEEPALIVE_FRAME: [u8; 8] = [0_u8; 8]` (`connection.rs:42`), written by the net-tick at `:1545`. It decodes to `total_len == 0` and MUST remain accepted; the cap comparison has to be `>` and not `>=`, and zero must not be rerouted into a refusal.
- MATERIAL FINDING 4 — `Error::LengthTooLarge`'s `Display` currently reads "distribution frame length does not fit usize" (`distribution/etf.rs:76-78`). Once the same variant also carries "over the maximum frame size", that string is wrong and must be reworded.
- REFUSAL VOCABULARY ALREADY SUFFICIENT: `connection.mark_down(ConnectionDownReason::ReadError)` is the existing arm used by both neighbouring failure paths (`:1474` overflow, `:1479` short read). No new public enum variant is required — see OQ-A.
- IN-HOUSE PRECEDENT for the constant: `crates/beamr/src/loader/decode/budget.rs:16`, `DEFAULT_DECODE_BYTE_BUDGET: usize = 64 * 1024 * 1024` — beamr's existing ceiling on bytes accepted from an untrusted source.
task:
DESIGN STANCE (decided, one fork carved as OQ-A): a documented max-frame constant enforced BEFORE any allocation at both framing sites, followed by a fallible reservation for the residual case. The wire format does not change, no size is negotiated, no knob is added, and no new public enum variant is minted.

D1 THE CONSTANT. `pub const MAX_DIST_FRAME_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024 * 1024;` in `crates/beamr/src/distribution/etf.rs`, alongside `MAX_ETF_DEPTH` and `PASS_THROUGH` (`:21-23`) — that module already owns distribution framing and is where `connection.rs` should import it from. PROVENANCE, TO BE STATED HONESTLY IN THE DOC COMMENT: OTP publishes no single hard maximum distribution frame size — the closest analogues are the `{packet, 4}` framing on the distribution socket and `+zdbbl` (distribution buffer busy limit, a send-side watermark, not a receive ceiling). So this constant is justified by INTERNAL CONSISTENCY, not by a mirrored OTP number: it equals `DEFAULT_DECODE_BYTE_BUDGET` (`loader/decode/budget.rs:16`), beamr's existing ceiling on bytes accepted from untrusted input. The doc comment must say exactly that rather than imply an OTP provenance the builder cannot cite. The builder must confirm no beamr subsystem legitimately sends a single frame above 64 MiB today (check `distribution/sender.rs` and the pg/global control paths) and record the check.

D2 THE LIVE LOOP (`connection.rs:1473-1478`). After the existing `checked_add` guard, and BEFORE any allocation: if `total_len > MAX_DIST_FRAME_BYTES`, `mark_down(ConnectionDownReason::ReadError)` and break — the same shape as the overflow arm immediately above it. Then replace `vec![0_u8; total_len]` with `Vec::new()` + `try_reserve_exact(total_len)` + `resize(total_len, 0)`, with the reservation failure taking the same mark-down-and-break arm. Cap first, fallible reservation second: the cap makes refusal deterministic and free, the reservation makes the residual (a 64 MiB allocation on a memory-starved box) graceful instead of an abort. NOTHING ELSE IN THE LOOP MOVES — the shutdown `select!`, the `note_inbound_activity` call, the EOF/`PeerClosed` classification and the `frame.split_at(control_len)` handler dispatch are byte-preserved.

D3 THE FRAMING HELPER (`etf.rs:146-152`). Same cap, before `try_reserve_exact`, refusing with the EXISTING `Error::LengthTooLarge`; its `Display` at `:76-78` is reworded to cover both causes (does not fit `usize` / exceeds the maximum frame size). No new `Error` variant, so no exhaustive-match sweep.

D4 WHAT THE REFUSAL COSTS THE PEER. The offending LINK is torn down through the existing connection-down path; the node, its scheduler, its processes and every other connection survive. That survival is the point of the finding and is walled explicitly in R3, not merely implied.

OQ-A RULED FOR v1 (recorded, revisitable): the refusal reuses `ConnectionDownReason::ReadError` rather than minting a dedicated `FrameTooLarge`. A dedicated variant would be more diagnosable, but `ConnectionDownReason` is a PUBLISHED cross-repo surface — it is documented in `docs/design/.../CONN-EVENTS-HOOK-SPEC.md` (whose arm table the review already flags as drifted, D6), it is re-exported from `distribution/connection_events.rs:102-126`, and it is consumed by frame's conn-down hook, where a new variant is a breaking exhaustive-match change. Minting it is a follow-on brief with a spec update and a consumer sweep, not a rider on a DoS fix. Adding the variant in THIS lane is a STOP.

requirements.title: RED — a peer-sized header is allocated unbounded, proven with a bounded header
requirements.spec: Per D1: two failing legs at the current bytes — one unit leg on the framing helper, one on the live read loop — both using a header just above the cap so the UNFIXED path's allocation stays small.
acceptance: BOUNDED-RED CONSTRAINT (load-bearing, must hold at every commit in this lane): the red legs claim `MAX_DIST_FRAME_BYTES + 1` bytes, NOT `0xFFFFFFFF`. At the unfixed bytes the code will actually perform that allocation, so the claimed size must stay bounded (~64 MiB, briefly held, then dropped). Asserting against a `0xFFFFFFFF`/`0xFFFFFFFF` header at RED would commit ~8 GiB or abort the test runner and is forbidden.

Leg A (framing helper, unit test in `distribution/etf.rs`): `read_dist_message` over a cursor whose 4-byte header claims `MAX_DIST_FRAME_BYTES + 1` with an empty body is asserted to return `Err(Error::LengthTooLarge)`. At current bytes it reserves ~64 MiB and returns `TruncatedBody` → RED.

Leg B (live read loop, unit test in `connection.rs`'s `mod tests`, using the existing `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) register_test_connection` helper at `:1400`): a pre-connected socket pair; the peer writes an 8-byte header claiming `MAX_DIST_FRAME_BYTES + 1` total and then WRITES NOTHING FURTHER, keeping the socket open. The connection is asserted to be marked down. At current bytes the loop allocates ~64 MiB and parks forever in `read_exact` on a body that never arrives, so the connection is NOT marked down → RED. The open-socket-no-body shape is what makes this leg discriminating rather than trivially passing on the short-read arm.

Leg B waits for the down transition through the existing event-driven connection-events subscription bounded by a SINGLE-SHOT `tokio::time::timeout` — not a retry loop, not a sleep-and-check. NO-POLLING applies to the wall as much as to the fix.

Leg C is GREEN-ONLY and must NOT be added or run during the red phase: a `0xFFFFFFFF`/`0xFFFFFFFF` header refused with zero allocation. It is only valid once the cap is in place; running it against unfixed bytes is a STOP.

requirements.title: MAX_DIST_FRAME_BYTES enforced before allocation at both framing sites
requirements.spec: Per D1/D2/D3: the documented constant in `etf.rs`; the cap-then-`try_reserve_exact` sequence in the live loop; the same cap in `read_dist_message`; the `Error::LengthTooLarge` Display reword.
acceptance: `MAX_DIST_FRAME_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024 * 1024` is a plain `const` with a doc comment stating the honest provenance (no OTP hard maximum exists; the value equals `DEFAULT_DECODE_BYTE_BUDGET`, beamr's existing untrusted-bytes ceiling) — no knob, no environment variable, no negotiated value, no per-connection option.

`connection.rs:1477`'s `vec![0_u8; total_len]` is gone: the cap check precedes any allocation and takes the existing `mark_down(ConnectionDownReason::ReadError)` + `break` arm; the surviving allocation is `Vec::new()` + `try_reserve_exact` + `resize`, with reservation failure taking the same arm. R1 legs A and B GREEN.

`read_dist_message` applies the same cap before `try_reserve_exact`, refusing with the EXISTING `Error::LengthTooLarge`; its `Display` at `etf.rs:76-78` is reworded to cover both causes. No new `Error` or `DecodeError` variant is minted, so no exhaustive-match sweep is required — confirm with `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` rather than assuming.
`ConnectionDownReason` is byte-unchanged: no new variant, `connection_events.rs` untouched, `CONN-EVENTS-HOOK-SPEC.md` untouched, frame's conn-down consumer unaffected (OQ-A).

The read loop is otherwise byte-preserved: the shutdown `tokio::select!` and its pre-enabled `Notified`, `note_inbound_activity`, the `UnexpectedEof` → `PeerClosed` classification, and the `frame.split_at(control_len)` handler dispatch are unchanged.

requirements.title: Permanent walls — keepalive, boundary, node-survival, and the prohibition grep
requirements.spec: The R1 legs become permanent, joined by the boundary cases the cap could plausibly break and a node-survival leg proving the blast radius is one link.
acceptance: KEEPALIVE WALL: an 8-byte all-zero `KEEPALIVE_FRAME` (`total_len == 0`) is still accepted, still refreshes the inbound-liveness clock, and does NOT mark the connection down. A `>=` cap comparison must make this wall red — state that in the test's comment so the boundary direction is pinned, not incidental.
BOUNDARY WALL: a frame of EXACTLY `MAX_DIST_FRAME_BYTES` is accepted and delivered to the control-frame handler intact; `MAX_DIST_FRAME_BYTES + 1` is refused. Both directions, one test.

NODE-SURVIVAL WALL (the finding's actual claim): with two live connections, an over-cap header on the first tears down ONLY that link — the second connection stays up, the manager keeps serving, and the host process does not abort. This is the wall that distinguishes the fix from merely converting an abort into a different abort.
GREEN-ONLY EXTREME LEG (R1 leg C, added now): a `0xFFFFFFFF`/`0xFFFFFFFF` header is refused with zero allocation, proving the cap fires before any reservation is attempted.

PROHIBITION GREP (added to the lane's gate evidence and runnable standalone): `crates/beamr/src/distribution/**` contains no `vec![0_u8; …]` / `vec![0u8; …]` whose length derives from peer-supplied bytes, and no allocation from a wire length that is not preceded by a `MAX_DIST_FRAME_BYTES` check.

FAIL-FIRST RECORDED: revert the R2 commit → the boundary wall, the node-survival wall and R1 legs A/B go red → restore. The revert transcript must show the reverted run still bounded (~64 MiB peak), never an 8 GiB commit.

boundaries: BOUNDED RED IS ABSOLUTE: red legs claim `MAX_DIST_FRAME_BYTES + 1`, never `0xFFFFFFFF`. No test, probe, or scratch binary in this lane may cause a multi-gigabyte allocation or an `handle_alloc_error` abort to demonstrate the defect. The `0xFFFFFFFF` extreme leg is GREEN-ONLY and is added after the cap exists.

`ConnectionDownReason` GAINS NO VARIANT in this lane (OQ-A ruled). It is a published cross-repo surface — `distribution/connection_events.rs:102-126`, `CONN-EVENTS-HOOK-SPEC.md`, frame's conn-down hook consumer. A dedicated `FrameTooLarge` is a follow-on brief with a spec update and a consumer sweep. Minting it here is a STOP.

ZERO-LENGTH FRAMES STAY VALID: `KEEPALIVE_FRAME` decodes to `total_len == 0` and is the net-tick's liveness signal. A `>=` cap comparison, or any rerouting of zero-length frames into the refusal arm, is a STOP.

THE WIRE FORMAT DOES NOT CHANGE: no new header field, no negotiated maximum, no capability flag, no handshake extension. Peers running today's beamr and OTP must interoperate byte-identically for every frame under the cap.

SCOPE: the handshake path (`distribution/handshake.rs`) has its own framing and its own length handling and is NOT in this lane. If the re-pin turns up the same unbounded-allocation shape there, it is a finding for the handoff and a separate brief, not a widening of this one.
The cap is a documented `const`, not a knob: NO config knob, environment variable, `ConnectionManager` builder option, or `system_info` key.

ZERO new `#[allow]` of any kind; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside `cfg(test)`; no `_ =>` catch-all arms introduced to dodge an exhaustive match (`Error`, `DecodeError`, `ConnectionDownReason` are all exhaustively matched today and must stay that way).
NO-POLLING: the fix is a single pre-allocation bound, never a retry, backoff, or size-probing loop. The walls wait on connection events with SINGLE-SHOT deadlines, never sleep-and-recheck loops.

MERGE-ORDER NOTE (not a hard dependency): this lane edits `crates/beamr/src/distribution/etf.rs` at `read_dist_message` (`:146-152`), its `Error` `Display` (`:76-78`) and the module constants (`:21-23`); RF-002 edits the same file at `decode_atom` (`:627`) and adds a `DecodeError` variant. Different regions, textual-conflict risk only — whichever lands second rebases.
verification:
PIN-SHIFT RE-VERIFY FIRST, BEFORE ANY EDIT: re-confirm at the actual build base (not at a0359a2) that `distribution/connection.rs:1477` still reads `let mut frame = vec![0_u8; total_len];` with the `checked_add`-only guard at `:1473-1476`; that `spawn_read_lifecycle` (`:1432`) is still reached only from `register_connection` (`:1367`) and therefore still only post-handshake; that `KEEPALIVE_FRAME` (`:42`) is still 8 zero bytes; that `distribution/etf.rs:146-152` still `try_reserve_exact`s an uncapped peer `u32`; that `read_dist_message` still has no non-test callers; and that `Error::LengthTooLarge`'s Display at `:76-78` still reads "does not fit usize". Record any drift in the handoff before starting.

GATE BAR — the full release battery from `gates.json` at the FINAL head, all five legs green in one sitting: (1) `cargo fmt --all --check`; (2) `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` for BOTH closures, fresh (Compiling lines visible); (3) `cargo test --workspace`; (4) `cargo check -p beamr-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked`; (5) the wasm-tests leg (`wasm-bindgen-test-runner` + `cargo test --manifest-path crates/beamr-wasm/Cargo.toml --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked`). Plus the R3 prohibition grep and 10× isolation on the live-loop walls (they drive real sockets and the isolation run is what catches a flaky event wait).

FAIL-FIRST DEMONSTRATION at the final head: revert the R2 commit → R1 legs A and B, the boundary wall and the node-survival wall go red → restore. The reverted run must be observed to stay bounded (~64 MiB peak) — if it does not, the red was mis-sized and the lane stops until it is. Recorded with exact assertion text.

HANDOFF must carry: the landed `MAX_DIST_FRAME_BYTES` value with its honest-provenance doc sentence, the result of the D1 check that no beamr subsystem legitimately emits a frame above the cap, the `cargo check` confirmation that no new enum variant and therefore no exhaustive sweep was required, the OQ-A record (ReadError reused; `FrameTooLarge` deferred with its spec+consumer cost), any handshake-path finding turned up during the re-pin, and the confirmed re-pinned file:lines as built.
